expectation: Read a whole raster into memory
note: collect()

expectation: Read a rectangle given in map coordinates
note: query(extent = )

expectation: Read a rectangle given in pixel coordinates
note: adgl windows in map coordinates only, and a pixel window is what you have when the source has no geotransform

expectation: Read at a reduced size and let GDAL serve an overview
note: query(dim = )

expectation: Choose which bands to read
note: query(bands = )

expectation: Choose the R type the values arrive in
note: collect(type = )

expectation: Hold a raster lazily and only read what is drawn
note: as_grd() and plot()

expectation: Reproject a grid
note: warp()

expectation: Pin the reprojected grid by size or resolution or extent
note: warp(dim = resolution = extent = )

expectation: Notice a target extent that is all projection stretch
note: the flag is the distance across the extent, not its size: a global source into EPSG:3031 gives an extent 8e23 m across whose corners are all the north pole. Warned after the run with a dim, refused with a resolution, and quiet where GDAL clamps for itself

expectation: Give a PROJ pipeline instead of a target CRS
note: a pipeline is the escape hatch when the default transformation is wrong; PROJ::proj_trans_create takes one

expectation: Pass warp and transform options through to GDAL
note: adgl has options = for open and for creation but nothing for the warper

expectation: Read values at points rather than over a window
note: the most-used raster verb in terra's own examples after rast() itself

expectation: Choose the data type of the written file
note: write_to() takes the source's type

expectation: Overwrite a file that is already there
note: write_to() neither refuses nor overwrites deliberately, it just calls GDAL

expectation: Creation options
note: write_to(options = )

expectation: Build a VRT rather than a materialised file
note: already on the README's list

expectation: Reach a subdataset of a container format
note: src() errors with no bands and no layers and does not mention subdatasets

expectation: Read a colour table or palette
note: an engine gap in GDAL7 as well

expectation: Read a layer
note: src() then collect()

expectation: Run an SQL SELECT against the source
seen_in: sf::st_read(query) and vapour_read_fields(sql); pyogrio sql 24 + sql_dialect 17
note: src(sql = , dialect = ) in place of layer; query() narrows the result

expectation: Filter features by an attribute expression
note: query(where = )

expectation: Filter features by an arbitrary geometry rather than a rectangle
note: query(extent = ) takes four numbers; a mask takes a polygon, and GDAL has SetSpatialFilter for it

expectation: Filter features by a rectangle
note: query(extent = )

expectation: Read only some attribute columns
note: query(fields = ), though the narrowing happens in R rather than in the driver - both corpora expect the driver to do it

expectation: Take the first n features or skip the first n
note: limit is there, skip is not, and paging needs both

expectation: Choose the layer by name or by position
note: src(layer = )

expectation: Reproject the features themselves
note: query(crs = )

expectation: Read geometry without attributes or attributes without geometry
note: fields = drops attributes but the geometry always comes back

expectation: Control the geometry type coming out
note: a layer mixing POLYGON and MULTIPOLYGON is the common case this answers

expectation: Append to a layer or replace it
note: write_to() always creates

expectation: Ask how many features there are without reading them
note: src() reports it and report() says when it is unknown

expectation: Ask for the layer extent without reading features
note: src() reports it

expectation: Return a nodata value as missing rather than as data
seen_in: rasterio src.read(masked) 37 calls - its most-used argument; terra and stars mask by default
note: collect() and as_grd() mask by default; the decision pivots on type, since only a double has a missing value to put there

expectation: Read a window that runs past the edge and pad it
note: query(pad = TRUE); the padding is whole source pixels so it does not move the grid, and it needs type double

expectation: Read the mask itself rather than the values
note: the per-pixel validity, which is not the same question as the values

expectation: Choose an overview level explicitly
note: src(options = "OVERVIEW_LEVEL=2") - GDAL's own open option, which is why src() takes them

expectation: Iterate the source's own blocks or tiles
note: grout owns tiling

expectation: Create a raster from a dtype and a transform with no source
seen_in: rasterio.open(driver dtype count width height crs transform) 25 calls
note: adgl is IO over sources; GDAL7::gdal_create() is the answer and stays there

expectation: Hand back the Arrow stream rather than a materialised table
seen_in: geopandas to_arrow; pyogrio use_arrow 172, its single most-used argument
note: adgl reads through nanoarrow and then builds a tibble, so the stream is already there and is thrown away

expectation: Read the feature id, and read by it
note: always named fid, from GDAL's own FID column name; read by it with query(where = "fid IN (...)"), which GDAL's SQL takes on every driver

expectation: Know or choose the geometry column's name
note: always named geom on read; write_to(geometry_name = , fid_name = ) names both where the format stores them

expectation: Datetimes and time zones survive the read
note: adgl hands back whatever nanoarrow makes of GDAL's Arrow stream, never checked against a source with a zoned datetime field

expectation: Drop Z and M from geometries on read
note: small, and wk can do it after the fact

expectation: Tell GDAL what encoding a source is in
note: src(options = "ENCODING=...") is how GDAL itself takes it, so the open option covers it without a new argument
